from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Linear systems map inputs to target vectors.", "Matrix columns define the new coordinate space.", "We search for x mapping to b."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Linear Systems", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3]).scale(0.6)
        
        basis_v1 = Vector([1, 0.5], color=YELLOW)
        basis_v2 = Vector([-0.5, 1], color=BLUE)
        basis_group = VGroup(grid, axes, basis_v1, basis_v2)
        self.place_in_area(basis_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(grid), Create(axes))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(GrowArrow(basis_v1), GrowArrow(basis_v2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        target_b = Vector([0.5, 1.5], color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(target_b, 'B5')
        self.play(Create(target_b))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Column Space: The Reachable World", [
            "Column space is the span of matrix columns.",
            "It represents all possible transformation outcomes.",
            "Dependent columns collapse the reachable space."

        self.play(Create(plane))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Null space maps non-zero inputs to origin.", "It highlights ambiguity in the transformation.", "Information is lost along null space directions."]
        self.setup_layout("Null Space: The 'Ghost' Inputs", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup coordinate system
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a vector that maps to the zero vector.
        v_in = Vector(RIGHT + UP, color=YELLOW)
        v_label = MathTex("x", color=YELLOW).next_to(v_in.get_end(), UP)
        
        self.play(Create(v_in), Write(v_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(v_in.animate.scale(0), v_label.animate.set_opacity(0))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the set of all such vectors.
        line = Line(start=axes.c2p(-2, -2), end=axes.c2p(2, 2), color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Label this set as the null space.
        ns_label = Text("Null Space", font_size=20, color=BLUE).next_to(line.get_center(), RIGHT)
        self.play(Write(ns_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The inverse matrix reverses the transformation.",
            "Inverses exist only for bijective mappings.",
            "We reconstruct the original input from output."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Inverse Matrices: The Rewind Button", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(plane)
        
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(plane.c2p(1, 1))
        
        # Matrix transformations
        mat_fwd = [[0.5, 0.5], [-0.5, 0.5]]
        mat_inv = [[1, -1], [1, 1]]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        dot_fwd = dot.copy().apply_matrix(mat_fwd)
        self.play(Transform(dot, dot_fwd), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Flash(dot, color=BLUE, num_lines=10, flash_radius=0.3), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        dot_back = dot.copy().apply_matrix(mat_inv)
        self.play(Transform(dot, dot_back), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "No null space means the system is invertible.",
            "Incomplete column space creates unreachable targets.",
            "Inverse operations uniquely return to the start."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Summary", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual objects
        circle = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Place them
        self.place_at_grid(circle, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(circle), FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(FadeIn(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Rotate(dot, angle=PI, about_point=self.grid["B2"]))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Geometric Intuition of Linear Systems: Spaces and Inverses

sections.title: Visualizing Linear Systems (1 min)
sections.content: Introduce linear systems as transformations. A system Ax = b represents the search for an input vector 'x' that maps to a target vector 'b'. Visualize columns of 'A' as basis vectors that define the destination grid.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm (the matrix A) moving in 2D space. The system solves where to set the joint angles (x) to place the gripper at a target coordinate (b).

sections.title: Column Space: The Reachable World (1 min)
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the matrix columns—the set of all possible outcomes. If the columns are linearly independent, they span the full space. If they are dependent, the reach 'collapses' into a line or a point.
sections.example: A 2D drone can fly anywhere (full column space). If its motors are locked on a specific axis, it can only move along a line (a lower-dimensional column space).

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Ghost' Inputs (1 min)
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of non-zero inputs 'x' that map to the origin. These represent ambiguity or loss of information during the transformation.
sections.example: A 3D scanner (Matrix A) takes a 3D object and projects it into a 2D image. The 'Null Space' is the line of sight along which depth is lost; any object placed on that line results in the same 2D shadow.

sections.title: Inverse Matrices: The Rewind Button (1 min)
sections.content: Explain the inverse matrix A⁻¹ as a 'reversal' operation. This only exists if the mapping is bijective (non-zero determinant). Geometrically, this means we can uniquely 'undo' the transformation to return to the original input.
sections.example: A video compressor (A) makes a file smaller (mapping to a smaller space). The inverse (A⁻¹) is the decompressor that reconstructs the original video from the compressed data.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary (1 min)
sections.content: Connect the dots: If the Null Space contains only zero, the system is invertible. If the Column Space doesn't cover the whole target space, the system may have no solution (b is unreachable) or infinitely many (if b is in the column space).
sections.example: A summary animation showing a transformation (A) followed by its inverse (A⁻¹) returning to the start, highlighting that if there is a 'Null Space', the inverse path cannot be uniquely traced back.
